KIND: info
STATUS: open

BODY:
AJC projective-morphism demand ledger landed (phase 0)

Commit 1b7d1ff7b6 adds AlgebraicJacobian/Projective/DemandLedger.lean. The exact seam-facing proposition is Scheme.PointedPicSharpQuasiProjectivePieces: for every pointed smooth proper geometrically integral curve, picSharp is represented by an integer-indexed coproduct of H-quasi-projective pieces. Proved adapters consume it into PointedPicSharpRep and then the verbatim fgaPicardRepresentability conclusion; neither adapter takes an explicit representation-witness argument.

The sole open seam producer is pointedPicSharpQuasiProjectivePieces_demand. Existing CurveProjectivity, IsHQuasiProjective, Scheme.{0} IsHQuasiProjectiveWith carried O(1), FiniteInAffine transport/aggregation, and Over coproduct assembly are inventory, not duplicated APIs. At Scheme.{0}, the carried certificate is already the faithful very-ample output; no IsVeryAmple alias is introduced.

The only conditional Proj demands currently justified are sectionGradedRing_gcommRing_demand and sectionGradedRing_gradedRing_demand, needed before mathlib Proj can consume the existing section direct sum. No general relative-Proj gluing or ample predicate is authorized until a narrower Picard consumer elaborates. In particular, ampleness must not be defined tautologically as a very-ample power, and the whole degree-graded Picard coproduct must not be strengthened to projective.

Ownership boundary with ajc-kleiman-rewire was agreed and archived in I-1822. Roadmap: AJC.picrep.projective-infra and children.

horizon: Review correction: 1b7d1ff7b6 adds a typed demand ledger, not a producer. Measured strict binders stay 37 while RepresentableBy lines rise 220 to 223; the witness is embedded inside H. Both adapters are standard-axiom conceptual H-consumers, while the terminal demand and both section-Proj demands each expose sorryAx. Producer movement is +0, and section-Proj is not connected to H. Read commit/task wording about an exact producer as stating the open demand only, with no reduction credit.
horizon: Classification correction after independent review (I-1826): commit 1b7d1ff7b6/c7bcebbed2 is a typed open producer statement plus two conditional adapters, not a producer or seam reduction. H packages the representation witness. Measured movement is sorry-free producers +0, seam reductions +0, and strict representation-witness binders +0. All three demand theorems retain sorryAx, and the conditional section-Proj gaps remain disconnected from H.

     9	/-!
    10	# Demand ledger for projective-morphism infrastructure
    11	
    12	This file records the projective infrastructure demanded by the Picard
    13	representability seam.  It is a ledger, not a second projectivity API.
    14	
    15	## The seam-facing demand
    16	
    17	`Scheme.PointedPicSharpRep` asks for a representing scheme that is locally of
    18	finite type and satisfies `Scheme.FiniteInAffine`.  It does not ask for a line
    19	bundle.  The existing project-local route supplies those two side conditions
    20	from a coproduct of H-quasi-projective pieces:
    21	
    22	* `Scheme.Hom.IsHQuasiProjective` is the universe-polymorphic embedding
    23	  predicate from `Picard/ProjectiveMorphismBasic.lean`;
    24	* `Scheme.locallyOfFiniteType_sigma` and
    25	  `Scheme.finiteInAffine_over_sigma_of_isHQuasiProjective` aggregate the two
    26	  side conditions in `Picard/QuasiProjectiveFiniteInAffine.lean`;
    27	* at `Scheme.{0}`, `Scheme.Hom.IsHQuasiProjective.exists_isHQuasiProjectiveWith`
    28	  adds a carried pullback of `O(1)`.  Thus the existing
    29	  `IsHQuasiProjectiveWith` is already the required very-ample output; defining
    30	  an alias named `IsVeryAmple` would only re-spell it.
    31	
    32	The open terminal producer demand is therefore
    33	`pointedPicSharpQuasiProjectivePieces_demand`: if proved, it would construct the
    34	representing coproduct and prove H-quasi-projectivity piecewise.  The two proved
    35	adapters below are only typing and consumption checks.  They both assume `H`,
    36	whose closed proposition packages the representation witness; they produce no
    37	representation and do not reduce the current seam debt.  Their signatures add
    38	no explicit `RepresentableBy` argument.
    39	
    40	## Conditional section-Proj route
    41	
    42	Mathlib's `AlgebraicGeometry.Proj` is the Proj of an `N`-graded commutative
    43	ring, with `Proj.toSpecZero`, `Proj.map`, and `Proj.fromOfGlobalSections`.  It is
    44	not a relative Proj of a sheaf of graded algebras.  The project already builds
    45	the section components `Scheme.Modules.sectionDeg L`, their tensor-power
    46	multiplication, and a `DirectSum.GCommSemiring`.  The first missing statements
    47	needed even to instantiate Mathlib's `Proj` on that section ring are the two
    48	open declarations in the final section: a graded commutative ring structure and
    49	the canonical internal grading by the direct-sum summands.
    50	
    51	Those declarations are conditional infrastructure: the seam-facing producer
    52	above does not mention a section ring, relative Proj, or ampleness.  A general
    53	relative-Proj gluing theory or a general ample predicate must not be built until
    54	a Picard-piece construction exposes a narrower consumer.  The whole Picard
    55	scheme must also not be strengthened to `IsProjective`: its degree-graded
    56	coproduct is not quasi-compact, as recorded by
    57	`Picard/AmbientPicNotProper.lean` and `Scheme.PointedPicSharpRepProjective`.
    58	
    59	## Existing inputs
    60	
    61	Curve projectivity is already produced by
    62	`Adelic.isProjective_of_smoothProperGeometricallyIntegral`.  The carried
    63	`O(1)`, base-change and open-image transport, `FiniteInAffine` transport, and
    64	Over-coproduct assembly remain owned by the established Picard modules and are
    65	imported here read-only.
    66	-/
    67	
    68	open CategoryTheory Limits
    69	
    70	noncomputable section
    71	
    72	universe u
    73	
    74	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    75	namespace Scheme
    76	
    77	/-- The exact projective presentation that the pointed Picard reduction can
    78	consume at every universe: `picSharp` is represented by a coproduct of
    79	H-quasi-projective schemes over the ground field.
    80	
    81	The integer index records the intended degree pieces without introducing a
    82	second, currently nonexistent `picSharpDeg` functor.  This closed proposition
    83	contains the representation witness in its conclusion; no downstream theorem
    84	takes an explicit representation-witness argument.  This keeps the strict
    85	binder count unchanged, but it remains logically a representation assumption. -/
    86	def PointedPicSharpQuasiProjectivePieces : Prop :=
    87	  ∀ {K : Type u} [Field K] (E : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))),
    88	    ∀ [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 E.hom] [IsProper E.hom]
    89	      [GeometricallyIntegral E.hom],
    90	      HasRationalPoint E →
    91	        ∃ X : ℤ → Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)),
    92	          Nonempty ((PicScheme.picSharp E).RepresentableBy (∐ X)) ∧
    93	            ∀ d, (X d).hom.IsHQuasiProjective
    94	
    95	/-- A piecewise H-quasi-projective representation supplies exactly the local
    96	finite type and `FiniteInAffine` conjuncts of `PointedPicSharpRep`.
    97	
    98	This is the seam-side typecheck for the ledger, not producer movement. -/
    99	theorem pointedPicSharpRep_of_quasiProjectivePieces
   100	    (H : PointedPicSharpQuasiProjectivePieces.{u}) :
   101	    PointedPicSharpRep.{u} := by
   102	  intro K _ E _ _ _ hpt
   103	  obtain ⟨X, hrep, hX⟩ := H E hpt
   104	  refine ⟨∐ X, hrep, ?_, ?_⟩
   105	  · exact locallyOfFiniteType_sigma X fun d => (hX d).locallyOfFiniteType
   106	  · exact finiteInAffine_over_sigma_of_isHQuasiProjective X hX
   107	
   108	/-- Conditional on the open ledger demand, the central seam follows verbatim,
   109	with no rational point binder on the target theorem.  This adapter is not a
   110	sorry-free producer or a discharge of the seam. -/
   111	theorem fgaPicardRepresentability_of_quasiProjectivePieces
   112	    {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
   113	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
   114	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom]
   115	    (H : PointedPicSharpQuasiProjectivePieces.{u}) :
   116	    (∃ X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)),
   117	        Nonempty ((PicScheme.picEt C).RepresentableBy X) ∧
   118	          LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom ∧ IsSeparated X.hom) ∧
   119	      (HasRationalPoint C → IsIso (PicScheme.picEtComparison C)) :=
   120	  fgaPicardRepresentability_of_pointedPicSharpRep C
   121	    (pointedPicSharpRep_of_quasiProjectivePieces H)
   122	
   123	/-- **Open terminal demand.** Construct the pointed Picard representer as a
   124	coproduct of H-quasi-projective pieces.  This is the only sorry in the
   125	seam-facing part of the demand ledger. -/
   126	theorem pointedPicSharpQuasiProjectivePieces_demand :
   127	    PointedPicSharpQuasiProjectivePieces.{u} := by
   128	  sorry
   129	
   130	end Scheme
   131	
   132	namespace Scheme.Modules
   133	
   134	variable {X : Scheme.{u}}
   135	
   136	/-- **Conditional section-Proj demand 1.** Upgrade the already-built graded
   137	commutative semiring on the section components of an invertible sheaf to the
   138	graded commutative ring required by Mathlib's `Proj`. -/
   139	theorem sectionGradedRing_gcommRing_demand (L : X.Modules) [IsInvertibleGr L] :
   140	    Nonempty (DirectSum.GCommRing (sectionDeg L)) := by
   141	  sorry
   142	
   143	/-- **Conditional section-Proj demand 2.** The canonical summands of the
   144	section-ring direct sum form an internal `N`-grading.  Together with
   145	`sectionGradedRing_gcommRing_demand`, this is the data needed for the term
   146	`AlgebraicGeometry.Proj` to elaborate on the section ring. -/
   147	theorem sectionGradedRing_gradedRing_demand (L : X.Modules) [IsInvertibleGr L]
   148	    (hR : DirectSum.GCommRing (sectionDeg L)) :
   149	    letI := hR
   150	    Nonempty (GradedRing (fun n => AddMonoidHom.range
   151	      (DirectSum.of (fun m => sectionDeg L m) n))) := by
   152	  sorry
   153	
   154	end Scheme.Modules
   155	end AlgebraicGeometry

events.text: The live consumer row confirms that projective infrastructure is only one slice of a much longer Picard-piece construction; I won’t claim that a section-ring lemma alone moves the seam. Still, the ledger’s two section-ring gaps may be independently closable and become the frozen core for a later concrete Proj consumer. I’m checking whether those are genuine proofs or merely missing instances, and whether the project already has a route from them to an actual scheme.

---
name: leansearch
description: Find existing lemmas/definitions before proving — the local `horizon search` index plus the Lean LSP MCP search tools (LeanSearch/Loogle/state-search/hammer-premise). Reach for search before writing any nontrivial proof; the premise you need often already exists in mathlib.
---

**Search before you prove.** Most facts you need already exist in mathlib or the
workspace. Searching is far cheaper than reproving. Use the local index first
(unlimited, instant), then the LSP search tools for broader semantic/type search.

## Local first: `horizon search`

An offline declaration search over `external_libraries` (mathlib by default) plus
the workspace's own projects. No GPU, API key, or network. Three modes share one
cached index:

- Natural language — what a lemma says:
  `horizon search "continuous function on a compact set attains its maximum"`
- `--name` — find a declaration by partial name:
  `horizon search --name isCompact.image`
- `--type` — find by shape of the statement; `?a`/`?b`/`_` are wildcards:
  `horizon search --type "Continuous ?f -> IsCompact ?s -> IsCompact (?f '' ?s)"`

Useful flags: `-n K`, `--lib NAME`, `--json`, `--reindex`. If results look thin,
run the project build so sources are current, then `horizon search --reindex`.

## Lean LSP MCP search tools

The `lean-lsp` MCP server (configured in `.mcp.json`) exposes a full search
arsenal. Rate limits are **per-tool** (separate pools), not a shared budget.

| Tool | Use it for | Limit |
|------|-----------|-------|
| `lean_local_search` | exact/partial declaration name; workspace + mathlib | unlimited |
| `lean_leansearch` | **semantic search by mathematical meaning** (PKU LeanSearch) | 10 / 30s |
| `lean_loogle` | search by **type shape** when you know the signature, not the name | remote; unlimited in `--loogle-local` |
| `lean_state_search` | lemmas that apply to a specific **proof state** (goal at a line) | 3 / 30s |
| `lean_hammer_premise` | **premise names** to feed `simp only [...]` / `aesop` / `grind` | 3 / 30s |
| `lean_leanfinder` | semantic fallback — only when `lean_leansearch` fails | 10 / 30s |

### Priority / escalation order

1. `lean_local_search("name")` — always first; unlimited, instant, deterministic.
2. `lean_leansearch("describe the math.")` — primary semantic search (see below).
3. `lean_loogle("?a -> ?b")` — simple type patterns only.
4. `lean_state_search(file, line, col)` — goal-conditioned lookup when stuck.
5. `lean_hammer_premise(file, line, col)` — premises for `simp`/`aesop`/`grind`.
6. `lean_leanfinder("description")` — last-resort semantic fallback.

### `lean_leansearch` — the PKU semantic tool (use it well)

LeanSearch (leansearch.net, from the PKU team) augments each mathlib theorem into
an informal description and matches your query against those embeddings —
returning the **nearest neighbours**, not just exact hits. That is its strength:
a theorem 90% of what you need is often enough; prove the small gap yourself.

- **Describe the mathematical content, not the name.** Query must end with `.`/`?`.
  - Good: `lean_leansearch("The image of a compact set under a continuous map is compact.")`
  - Good (mixed): `lean_leansearch("natural numbers. from: n < m, to: n + 1 < m + 1")`
  - Weak: `lean_leansearch("add_comm")` → use `lean_local_search` instead.
  - Weak: `lean_leansearch("∀ (a b : ℕ), a + b = b + a")` → use `lean_loogle` instead.
- **Trust a negative result.** If a precise, mathematically accurate description
  returns nothing relevant, the theorem likely isn't in mathlib — stop rephrasing
  and prove it (or find another route) rather than searching endlessly.

### `lean_loogle` — type-shape search

Searches by *type structure*, not names. Syntax: `?a`/`?b` type vars, `_`
wildcards, `->`/`→` arrows, `|- pattern` by conclusion.
- Good: `lean_loogle("(?a -> ?b) -> List ?a -> List ?b")` → `List.map`
- Anti-pattern: nested `Submodule`/`LinearMap`/`Finsupp`, 3+ typeclass
  constraints, or guessy implicit structure — use `lean_leansearch` for those.

## Discipline

- Treat every hit as a **candidate**: read the signature/source and confirm with
  the Lean checker (see the `lean-check` skill) before depending on it.
- Try multiple phrasings — project name, mathematical concept, conclusion/type.
- Local (`horizon search` / `lean_local_search`) is optimized for the checked-out
  sources here; the LSP tools reach broader mathlib precedent. Use both.

     6	module
     7	
     8	public import Mathlib.Algebra.DirectSum.Module
     9	public import Mathlib.Algebra.Module.Submodule.Basic
    10	
    11	/-!
    12	# Decompositions of additive monoids, groups, and modules into direct sums
    13	
    14	## Main definitions
    15	
    16	* `DirectSum.Decomposition ℳ`: A typeclass to provide a constructive decomposition from
    17	  an additive monoid `M` into a family of additive submonoids `ℳ`
    18	* `DirectSum.decompose ℳ`: The canonical equivalence provided by the above typeclass
    19	
    20	
    21	## Main statements
    22	
    23	* `DirectSum.Decomposition.isInternal`: The link to `DirectSum.IsInternal`.
    24	
    25	## Implementation details
    26	
    27	As we want to talk about different types of decomposition (additive monoids, modules, rings, ...),
    28	we choose to avoid heavily bundling `DirectSum.decompose`, instead making copies for the
    29	`AddEquiv`, `LinearEquiv`, etc. This means we have to repeat statements that follow from these
    30	bundled homs, but means we don't have to repeat statements for different types of decomposition.
    31	-/
    32	
    33	@[expose] public section
    34	
    35	
    36	variable {ι R M σ : Type*}
    37	
    38	open DirectSum
    39	
    40	namespace DirectSum
    41	
    42	section AddCommMonoid
    43	
    44	variable [DecidableEq ι] [AddCommMonoid M]
    45	variable [SetLike σ M] [AddSubmonoidClass σ M] (ℳ : ι → σ)
    46	
    47	/-- A decomposition is an equivalence between an additive monoid `M` and a direct sum of additive
    48	submonoids `ℳ i` of that `M`, such that the "recomposition" is canonical. This definition also
    49	works for additive groups and modules.
    50	
    51	This is a version of `DirectSum.IsInternal` which comes with a constructive inverse to the
    52	canonical "recomposition" rather than just a proof that the "recomposition" is bijective.
    53	
    54	Often it is easier to construct a term of this type via `Decomposition.ofAddHom` or
    55	`Decomposition.ofLinearMap`. -/
    56	class Decomposition where
    57	  decompose' : M → ⨁ i, ℳ i
    58	  left_inv : Function.LeftInverse (DirectSum.coeAddMonoidHom ℳ) decompose'
    59	  right_inv : Function.RightInverse (DirectSum.coeAddMonoidHom ℳ) decompose'
